item.title: Latinos & Latinas Run Club — Thu Aug 6, 6:30 PM — The Glass Jug Downtown
item.description:
Come connect with us over a run! Hosted by Latinos Run and Latinas Run of Raleigh & Durham, all paces and people are welcome weekly starting at 6:30pm. We’ll follow a 3–4 mile route through downtown Durham before returning to us here at Glass Jug Downtown for drinks and camaraderie. Latinos Run and Latinas Run are nationwide running organizations dedicated to empowering and connecting communities through running, wellness, and culture. Their mission is to create a supportive, inclusive space where individuals of all backgrounds and fitness levels feel welcomed and encouraged to move their bodies and build meaningful connections. You can learn more about the organizations here: https://www.latinasrunclub.com/ and https://www.latinosrun.com/ We aim to be a welcoming space for runners to connect, move, and enjoy each other’s company – so join us, Latinos Run, and Latinas Run every Thursday! View on Facebook.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Intermediate Stained Glass: Experience Required, Fall Themes — Sat Aug 8, 3:00 PM — Fusion Gallery
item.description:
This is a three-hour class in which students will build on the basics of the copper foil or “Tiffany” method of creating stained glass. This process includes cutting, grinding, foiling, and soldering individual glass pieces. Students will also learn to work with tinned copper wire to create fine details and flourishes. All materials are included in class pricing.

item.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Aug 8, 4:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Downtown Durham True Crime Walking Tour — Sat Aug 8, 6:00 PM — Lucky Strike Tower
item.description:
From mayoral candidates turned murder suspects, to terrifying cult leaders, to dramatic gangster dramas. Join us on the guided Durham True Crime Tour, hosted by a local historian, and explore the dark side of Durham’s history.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Aug 8, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Bull City Treasure Hunt — Sun Aug 9, 8:00 AM — Durham Central Park
item.description:

This market is a safe place for everyone to come and enjoy themselves! Kick back on the lawn and listen to some tunes spun by our DJ, grab a cute little beverage, and explore the vendor booths! You never know what treasure will await you!

item.description: A Summer Intensive for Theatre Lovers Ages 10-17 Back by popular demand! We’re thrilled to announce that Next Stop Broadway® will return to DPAC this summer from August 10-14, 2026. Next Stop Broadway® is a week-long program consisting of classes, workshops, and rehearsals focused on classic Broadway shows. A staff of Broadway professionals teach participants songs and choreography from hit shows from the “Golden Age of Broadway,” and participants work together throughout the week to create unique skits. The program culminates with an “Opening Night” performance for family and friends on DPAC’s stage. This summer intensive encourages teamwork and is designed to teach the importance of building a strong Ensemble. All participants are part of the Ensemble; no auditions are required, and there are no “lead” roles. item.title: Hematology Case Conference: — Tue Aug 11, 8:00 AM — Duke South
item.description:
This weekly conference is held each Tuesday from 8-9 a.m. and includes case-based presentations on a wide variety of topics in hematology. In general, discussion will cover inpatient and outpatient problems, with an emphasis on including primary radiographic data, clinical laboratory results and pathology specimens for review. Several recent articles relevant to the discussion will be presented with each case, with an emphasis on recent research (clinical, translational and basic).

item.title: Whose Paper Is It Anyway? Good and Questionable Authorship Practices — Tue Aug 11, 2:00 PM — None
item.description:
REGISTRATION: Click Here
NOTE: Registration closes 24 hours before event start. Please register ahead of the event. Registrants will receive Zoom information and related materials by email one week and within 24 hours before the event.
Reserve your seat in the virtual Research Integrity Roundtable "Whose Paper Is It Anyway? Good and Questionable Authorship Practices" on August 11th, 2026 from 2:00 pm - 3:30 pm. Participants will learn about good and questionable authorship practices, the Duke guidelines regarding authorship, and what to do when you have an authorship dispute. A case study will be discussed in breakout rooms.
This event is only open to current Duke faculty, staff, and students. Attending this event fulfills the RCR-200 requirement for Faculty and Staff as well as the 714 RCR credit for graduate students, but participants must attend for at least 60 minutes to receive credit.
Contact: ASIST asist@duke.edu
Source: Duke University

item.description:

These sessions allow you space to slow down, reflect, and grow in gratitude in an online group setting. The Mini Mental Makeovers are led by Laurie Kovens, a Senior EAP Counselor with PAS. She is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and a Certified Employee Assistance Professional, with over 15 years of experience.
These sessions are not recorded to maintain privacy and ensure safety when sharing thoughts or experiences.

item.title: Foundations of Water Education, 12 lessons — Tue Aug 18, 9:00 AM — Goose Creek State Park
item.description:
The Foundations of Water Education Guide from Project WET features 12 of its most popular, hands-on activities designed to build water literacy in students. Covering key topics like watersheds, groundwater, ecology, and water resource management, these engaging lessons align with the Principles of Water Literacy to deepen understanding of our most vital resource. Each activity includes step-by-step instructions, academic correlations, and interactive learning experiences that foster critical thinking and problem-solving. This essential guide lays the groundwork for water education, with more resources coming soon to expand on Project WET’s comprehensive curriculum.
To register: Email Monique.McKoy@ncparks.gov

Join us at Mayo River State Park for a kayaking trip along the river!
We will be meeting at the Mayo River 220 Business Access (Mayo River Bridge Kayak Launch 3100-3110 US-220 BUS, Stoneville, NC 27048). Cars will be left there as we commute to the Anglin Mill Access to launch the kayaks. Depending on the water levels, the trip can last 2 to 4 hours. Wear clothing that you're comfortable being in water with. Dry bags, sunscreen, hats, water, snacks, and your own lifejackets if you have them are all recommended. We will have spare lifejackets just in case.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather or muddy waters. Message the email below to register as we have limited spaces. We will max out the event at 6 people.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Headwaters Festival — Sat Aug 22, 11:00 AM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
The Elk Knob Community Heritage Organization (EKCHO) announces that the 19th annual Headwaters Community Day Festival will return to Elk Knob State Park on Saturday, August 22nd, 2026 from 11am to 3pm. The Headwaters Community Day Festival is a gathering to celebrate the area’s unique culture and foodways. The activities start at 11 am and include live music, local crafters, farmers, and other artisans demonstrating their work. At noon, the High Country’s largest potluck dinner will be served, featuring dozens of local dishes. The public is encouraged to bring their own dish to share. Elk Knob Community Heritage Organization (EKCHO) is a 501c(3) organization that is sponsoring the festival in partnership with Elk Knob State Park. For more information contact Jan Ellison, president of the Elk Knob Community Heritage Organization (EKCHO) at EKCHO@gmail.com. The event is free and open to the public.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: *IN-PERSON* SF/F Group — Tue Aug 25, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Durham Writers Group We will be at the Moon House at 3039 University Dr. in Durham. This venue does not serve food or drink, but feel free to bring your own. There is a kitchenette for our use, but be sure to clean up afterwards. The space might be a little cozy; please consider masking or staying home if you have a respiratory ailment.
This sub-group focuses on Speculative Fiction, including Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror. If you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.
Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. Next, we have a 5 minute Free-For-All discussion about the work -- then the author may speak. (We usually get through three readers.)

item.title: AI Storm Readiness Summit: Cybersecurity in the AI Era — Thu Aug 27, 8:30 AM
item.description: Cloud Security Alliance Triangle Chapter **The storm of vulnerability disclosures from Project Glasswing is the first of many large waves of AI-discovered vulnerabilities that may occur in rapid sequence.** Throughout this summit, attendees will have the opportunity to examine how advances in AI are reshaping the cybersecurity landscape by dramatically increasing the likelihood that attackers can discover new vulnerabilities, develop novel exploits, and execute complex automated attacks at scale. While AI is also accelerating vulnerability remediation and improving software quality, security leaders are facing a growing asymmetry: the inherent limitations of patching, operational constraints, and expanding attack surfaces create a heavier burden for defenders than for attackers. item.description:
